resources.string: Section 19 of the Constitution gives every adult South African citizen the right to vote in free, fair and regular elections, and to do so in secret.
You are a South African citizen.
You are 18 or older on election day. You may register from 16.
You are on the voters\' roll in the voting district where you live.
You have a valid South African ID on the day.
Valid temporary ID certificate from Home Affairs
Not accepted: passport or driver\'s licence
Lost your ID? Apply at Home Affairs for a temporary ID certificate before voting day.
Stations open at 07:00 and close at 21:00. If you are in the queue by 21:00, you may still vote.
An official checks your ID and finds your name on the voters\' roll.
Your thumbnail is marked with indelible ink so nobody can vote twice.
You get stamped ballot papers. Make one mark next to your choice inside a voting booth.
Fold your ballots and drop them in the ballot box while officials and party agents watch the box, never your choice.
National and provincial elections (3 ballots since 2024)
National ballot: parties for the 200 compensatory seats in the National Assembly
Regional ballot: parties and independent candidates for your province\'s National Assembly seats
Provincial ballot: parties and independent candidates for your provincial legislature
Ward ballot: the councillor who represents your ward
PR ballot: a party for your municipal council
District ballot: in areas with a district council
Your rights at the voting station
Nobody may watch you mark your ballot or force you to say who you voted for.
The Electoral Code of Conduct bans intimidation, bribery and violence. Nobody may pay, threaten or force you to vote a certain way.

If you have a disability or cannot read, a companion of your choice aged 18 or older, or the presiding officer, may help you vote. Blind and partially sighted voters can ask for the Universal Ballot Template.

If illness, disability, pregnancy, old age or work keeps you from your station on election day, apply for a special vote during the IEC\'s application period. Officials visit you at home, or you vote at your station on the special voting days before election day.

In national elections, registered voters overseas can vote at a South African embassy, high commission or consulate after notifying the IEC (form VEC10) before the deadline. Local government elections cannot be voted in from abroad.
Report a problem or electoral offence
Tell the presiding officer at your station first. You can also call the IEC Contact Centre, toll-free, or report crimes such as intimidation to the SAPS.
Source: Constitution of South Africa (s19), Electoral Act 73 of 1998 and the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC).

I can\'t sign in. What should I do?
Check that your 13-digit ID number is correct. For the face check, find good light, remove sunglasses or a hat, and hold the phone at eye level with your whole face in the frame.
After 3 face checks that don\'t match, sign-in pauses for 15 minutes to protect your account. Wait for the timer, then try again in good light.
How do I vote in the app?
Tap Vote now on Home. Choose a party on each of the three ballots, check your choices on the Review screen, then confirm with a quick face check.
Yes, until you confirm. On the Review screen, tap Change next to any ballot. Once your face check passes, your vote is cast and cannot be changed.
After voting, tap View vote receipt on Home. Each ballot has a receipt code you can use to check that it was recorded. Receipts never show who you voted for.
How do I get election reminders?
Go to Settings and turn on Election Reminders, then choose when to be reminded, from a month before to the morning of voting day. Allow notifications when your phone asks.
How do I change the language?
Tap the language button (EN) at the top of Home, or go to Settings and tap Language. The app is available in English, Afrikaans, isiZulu and isiXhosa.
How do I update my phone number or address?

Open Voter Profile from Settings and edit your cellphone or address. Changing your name or ID number needs a face check first. If you moved, also re-register with the IEC so you vote at the right station.

At the voting station in the district where you registered. Find my voting station shows the nearest likely station to your address. Confirm the official one by SMSing your ID number to 32810 or dialling *120*432#.
Which ID can I use to vote?
A green barcoded ID book, a smart ID card, or a valid temporary ID certificate from Home Affairs. Passports and driver\'s licences are not accepted.
What if I can\'t get to my voting station?

Apply for a special vote during the IEC\'s application period, online at elections.org.za or at your local IEC office. Special votes are cast in the days before election day, at home or at your station.
Can I vote if I\'m overseas?
Only in national elections. If you are registered, notify the IEC online (form VEC10) before the deadline, then vote at a South African embassy, high commission or consulate.

Yes. If you have a disability or cannot read, a person you choose who is 18 or older, or the presiding officer, may assist you. Blind and partially sighted voters can ask for the Universal Ballot Template.
How do I check that I\'m registered?
SMS your ID number to 32810 (R1 per SMS), dial *120*432#, or use My Registration Details on elections.org.za. You can check your app details under Check my registration on Home.
I moved. What do I need to do?

Re-register at your new address so you are on the right voters\' roll. Do it online at elections.org.za or at your local IEC office before the roll closes, which happens when an election is proclaimed.
I lost my ID. Can I still vote?
Yes, if you get a temporary ID certificate from Home Affairs before voting day and are on the voters\' roll. Apply early, as offices are busy close to elections.
Can anyone see who I voted for?
No. Your ballots are stored against a one-time voting token, not your name or ID number. Receipts confirm that a ballot was recorded, never which party you chose.
What personal information does the app keep?

Your name, ID number, ID photos, face template, address and cellphone number, used only to register you and confirm it is you. Under POPIA you may ask to see or correct this information through Report a problem.
What happens to my face scan?

Your face is turned into a numeric template on your phone. Only that template is stored, and it is used only to confirm it is you when you sign in and before your vote is cast. It is never linked to your ballot choices.
